slides.title: Lead with outcomes, not jargon
bullets: First point — explain the benefit in everyday language
Second point — use an analogy before an acronym
Third point — one idea per slide keeps the room with you
Fourth point — fragments animate as you speak (try ← →)
slides.notes: Emphasize plain language. contentSlide: true adds the framed card surface.

slides.title: A key insight
slides.quote: Replace this with a quote, pull-out stat, or memorable one-liner that anchors the section.
slides.notes: Pause after the quote. Let it land before moving on.

slides.title: Build from JSON
slides.code:
# One command — branded HTML out
python scripts/build-reveal.py slides.json my-talk.html

# Slide types in JSON:
# title | section | content | table
# glossary | showcase | code | closing
slides.caption: See examples/demo-slides.json for the full schema.
slides.notes: Show the repo README. Mention /leafygreen-html-presentation skill in Cursor.

slides.title: Presenter shortcuts
bullets: ← → — previous / next slide
O — overview grid of all slides
S — speaker notes window (two-screen mode)
F — fullscreen · Esc — exit overview or notes
slides.notes: Demo S live if two screens available. Hash URLs work — share a link to a specific slide.

slides.title: Three things to remember
bullets: One file, full MongoDB branding, zero npm for the audience
JSON or HTML — pick your authoring path
Plain language + phrasebook = mixed rooms that stay engaged
